--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Ablation.get_effects()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: Get the results of the ablation as a table. twitter-card: title: >- [Ablation.get_effects()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Pointblank description: Get the results of the ablation as a table. title: >- [Ablation.get_effects()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Get the results of the ablation as a table. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the results of the ablation as a table. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/pointblank/blob/main/pointblank/ablation.py#L4138-L4266){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Ablation.get_effects() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The table has one row for each version of the training table and each metric: the full table first (as the baseline), then the variants. Use it to make plots, to compare ablations of different data, or to look at the metrics that the report doesn't show. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A Polars DataFrame (or a pandas DataFrame, if Polars isn't installed) with these columns: - `variant`, `name`, `strategy`: the variant's id, name, and strategy (`"full"` for the full table) - `steps`: the numbers of the steps whose failing rows were removed, as a list - `left_out`: for a variant of [`drop_all_but_each()`](`pointblank.Ablation.drop_all_but_each`), the step whose rows are kept - `group`: for a variant of [`drop_groups()`](`pointblank.Ablation.drop_groups`), the value of the group whose rows are removed, as a string - `sweep`, `value`: for a point of a sweep (from [`sweep_score()`](`pointblank.Ablation.sweep_score`) or [`sweep_step()`](`pointblank.Ablation.sweep_step`)), the id of the sweep and the point's value (the share of the scored rows removed, the score cutoff, or the value of the step's parameter) - `n_removed`, `f_removed`: the number and share of rows removed - `corruption`, `column`, `n_corrupted`, `checked_by`: for a variant of [`inject()`](`pointblank.Ablation.inject`), the defect (`"function"` for a function), the column it's put into (missing for `"duplicate"`), the number of rows corrupted (or copied), and the step that checks for it (`0` and missing for the other variants) - `metric`, `mean`, `sd`: the metric, and its mean and standard deviation across the repeats - `delta_vs_full`, `delta_vs_full_lower`, `delta_vs_full_upper`: the mean paired difference from the full table, with its interval at `conf_level=` - `p_vs_full`, `p_adj_vs_full`: the p-value of that difference, and the p-value adjusted across the variants (as set by `adjust=`) - `control_mean`: the mean of the metric for the variant's control - `delta_vs_control`, `delta_vs_control_lower`, `delta_vs_control_upper`, `p_vs_control`, `p_adj_vs_control`: the same, for the difference from the control - `delta_added`, `delta_added_lower`, `delta_added_upper`, `p_added`, `p_adj_added`: for a variant of `drop_all_but_each()`, the difference that removing the left-out step's rows makes on top of the other steps (the variant that removes every step's rows, compared with this variant, or with its control) - `verdict`: `"helps"`, `"hurts"`, or `"inconclusive"` for the metric named in `metric=` (missing for other metrics, and with fewer than 3 repeats), or `"redundant"` for a variant of `drop_all_but_each()` whose left-out step helps on its own but adds nothing to the other steps The comparisons are missing for the full table, and the control columns are missing when `control=None` (and for the variants of `inject()`, which remove no rows). The intervals and p-values need at least 2 repeats. The verdict of a `drop_all_but_each()` variant is based on the `delta_added` columns, that of an `inject()` variant on the `delta_vs_full` columns, and those of the other variants on the `delta_vs_control` columns (or the `delta_vs_full` columns, when `control=None`). The groups of steps that [`shapley()`](`pointblank.Ablation.shapley`) adds have the strategy `"shapley"` and no verdict, and their p-values are adjusted on their own; the Shapley values themselves are in [`get_shapley()`](`pointblank.Ablation.get_shapley`). ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Here's an ablation of a table of temperature readings with some out-of-range values. ::: {#f330fa38 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl temps = [20 + (k * 37 % 11 - 5) * 0.6 for k in range(300)] for k in range(0, 300, 25): temps[k] *= 10 readings = pl.DataFrame({"temp": temps}) def evaluate(train, *, seed, variant): sample = train.sample(fraction=1.0, with_replacement=True, seed=seed) return abs(sample["temp"].mean() - 20) validation = ( pb.Validate(data=readings) .col_vals_between(columns="temp", left=-10, right=45) .interrogate() ) ablation = ( pb.Ablation(validation, evaluate=evaluate, metric="error", higher_is_better=False) .drop_each() .run() ) ablation.get_effects().select("variant", "mean", "delta_vs_control", "verdict") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Removing the 12 rows that failed step 1 lowers the error by about 7 degrees compared with removing 12 random rows, so the verdict is that the step helps.
